question: what are the prereqs for intermediate accounting 1
answer:
ACCT 321 Intermediate Accounting I is 4 credits. Its prerequisite is ACCT 222 Principles of Managerial Accounting [2]. The Registrar says students are responsible for satisfactorily completing all prerequisites before registering. Review prerequisite requirements in Web Self Service and course descriptions there under “Course/Catalog Description.” Transfer or visiting students who have fulfilled the prerequisite but cannot register should contact the academic school offering the course. If you prove you satisfied it, the unit secretary may place an override on your record; then complete registration in Experience: https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/ [3].

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ACCT321) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/)

question: I'm an accounting major starting next fall. What accounting and econ classes should I take my first year and in what order?
answer:
The available Accounting BS recommended plan (Bachelor of Science) is for students admitted in 2026–2027; it does not establish the schedule for your next fall. question: what do i need to complete the economics minor? how many credits total
answer:
The Economics Minor (Minor) requires all four courses: ECON 101 MICROECONOMICS, ECON 102 INTRODUCTION TO MACROECONOMICS, ECON 311 INTERMEDIATE MICROECONOMICS, and ECON 312 INTERMEDIATE MACROECONOMICS; plus 2 electives selected from Economics (ECON) courses. [1]

The minor must include between 16 and 24 credits, including non-General Education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits. [5] The Economics Minor requirements page does not state an exact total credit count. [1]

To declare it, visit the Office of the Registrar or Center for Student Success for a major/minor declaration form, get the minor convener’s signature, then return the signed form to the Office of the Registrar. Do this after consulting your advisor and within a reasonable time before graduation. [11]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MN-ECON) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/)

question: does business statistics count as my math gen ed or do i still need a separate math class
answer:
I can’t verify that BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS counts for your individual Gen Ed requirement. The catalog names it as an elective for the Statistics Minor, but does not say it fulfills Quantitative Reasoning [2]. Ramapo requires one Quantitative Reasoning course, within your first 64 credits [5]. The catalog identifies MATH 108, MATH 100T, MATH 101, MATH 104, MATH 106, and MATH 110 as Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR) [16]. The Testing Center also says MATH 101/104/106/108 or PHIL106 are college-level courses that meet your General Education and/or major math requirement [13]. Check the approved-course list [10] and ask the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) to confirm whether you need another course based on your record; contact success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441 [12]. If you have completed 64 credits without completing or registering for college-level math Gen Ed, a registration hold applies until you register [12].

question: is there a 150 credit option or a masters in accounting so i can sit for the cpa exam
answer:
Yes. Ramapo’s Accounting MS, a Master of Science in the Anisfield School of Business, is 30 credits and prepares students for the CPA exam. In combination with an undergraduate degree, students would attain the 150 credits required to sit for the CPA examination. [1][2]

The Accounting Club’s advisors also encourage students to accumulate 150 undergraduate credits toward obtaining a Certified Public Accountant License. [4]

The MSAC has required courses and electives; see its catalog page: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MS-MSAC. [1] It offers spring, summer and fall start options. [2] For admissions questions, contact Graduate Admissions at graduate@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7270. [2][3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MS-MSAC) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/home/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/accounting-club/)

question: should i major in finance or accounting, which one gets better jobs
answer:
Ramapo lists both Accounting BS and Finance BS [1][2]. The Finance page names careers in financial analysis, stock brokerage, money management, real estate analysis, banking, insurance and risk management, and international finance [2]. The Accounting page describes work involving financial and managerial accounting, cost accounting, income taxes, planning, analysis and problem solving [1]. These pages don’t establish which major gets better jobs or compare employment outcomes, so I don’t have verified information to say one has better jobs.

For help choosing, the Center for Student Success recommends gathering information from the catalog, School events, advisors and students, and talking with faculty; it notes that job experience matters and recommends co-op or internship experience before graduation [8]. Contact Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207 [8].

The Cahill Career Development Center recommends connecting with faculty and visiting the Career Center to speak with a Career Advisor [3]. You can also explore career options and labor-market trends through O*NET [4], or use FOCUS 2 to explore careers and select a major; access code: ramapo430 [5]. Contact the Cahill Career Development Center at careercenter@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7444 (Main Office, C-209) or (201) 684-7675 (ASB Office, ASB-513) [3].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-ACCT) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-FNCE) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/asb-career-pathways/next-steps/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/)

question: what are the core business courses everyone in the anisfield school has to take, like the ones that arent specific to accounting or finance
answer:
The Accounting BS and Finance BS both list these required ASB courses, in addition to the accounting/finance-specific courses: ACCT 221 Principles of Financial Accounting; ACCT 222 Principles of Managerial Accounting; BADM 223 Business Law I; BADM 225 Management Statistics; BADM 495 Strategic Management; ECON 101 Microeconomics; ECON 102 Introduction to Macroeconomics; FINC 301 Corporate Finance I; INFO 224 Principles of Information Technology; MGMT 302 Managing Organizational Behavior; MGMT 370 Operations Management; and MKTG 290 Marketing Principles and Practices. [1][2]
Both programs also require one course from the ASB International Category and one from the ASB Ethics Category. [1][2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-ACCT) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-FNCE)
